html:
In 1605 and 1606 the Spanish governor Antonio de Osorio, on royal orders, forced the people of northern and western Hispaniola to move near Santo Domingo and burned their towns. Spain wanted to stop their trade with Dutch and English smugglers.

Thousands of people and their cattle were moved. Many died, and much of the livestock was lost or ran wild in the empty lands.

The policy backfired. French buccaneers moved into the west, hunting wild cattle, and settled there. By 1697 Spain recognised the French colony that became Saint-Domingue. The division of the island between Haiti and the Dominican Republic goes back to these burnings, which left Spanish Hispaniola small and poor.
